text:
**Short answer:** for most campers, a 250-500 Wh station is the sweet spot. It's light enough to carry and covers phones, lights, a camera and a CPAP for a weekend. If you need a fridge or bigger appliances, step up to about 1,000 Wh or more.

## Weekend and car camping (about 250-300 Wh)
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (about $249) is PowerStationGearLab's best overall for camping. It has 288 Wh of LiFePO4 and weighs 8.3 lb, but only 300 W of AC output. Its Amazon link is on [the review page](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/). Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so the Plus is only sold through retailers like Amazon.
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (about $269-299) has 286 Wh and a 600 W inverter, and it can expand to 572 Wh. Same [review page](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/).
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (about $199) has a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the AC-outlet version, not the "DC" variant. Same [review page](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/).
- **Bluetti Elite 30 V2** is TechRadar's budget pick: 288 Wh and 600 W, compact, with no built-in light ([TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)). It's $289.99, or $275.50 with code AFF5OFF: [buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-30-v2).

## Multi-day trips, fridge or van (about 1,000 Wh and up)
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** is OutdoorGearLab's top pick for off-grid camping. It weighs 39 lb, outputs 2,200 W, and testers measured 1,710 Wh usable. The list price is $1,499, but they say it can be found for under $900 on Amazon ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)).
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** is their best value, at under $530 on sale. It's compact but has a noisy fan ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)).
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** is TechRadar's camping pick ([TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)). PowerStationGearLab lists it at about $799.
- **Bluetti AC180** (1,152 Wh with the solar kit listed, 1,800 W) is $499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF: [buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180).
- **ALLPOWERS P1800** (1,024 Wh, 1,800 W) is $439, or $395.10 with code ALLPOWERS26: [buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-1024wh).

## Notes
- The Dealectric links go to the brands' official US stores. Dealectric earns a commission on purchases through them, at no extra cost to you. The codes were last tested on Oct 25, and checkout has the final word.
- I don't have direct purchase links for the Jackery, EcoFlow and Anker models, only the review pages above. Check current prices at Amazon or the brand's own store.
- TechRadar notes Black Friday and Cyber Monday are close, so prices may drop soon if you can wait.
- Turn off a CPAP's humidifier. It can triple the draw, and without it a 288 Wh unit runs most CPAPs 3-5 nights.
- These are too big for planes, since they all exceed the 100 Wh airline limit.

If you tell me what you'll run (CPAP, fridge, laptop?) and how many nights, I can narrow it to one pick.
